method: fresh shallow clone of the pinned commit; classify first (protocol/tool schema, session semantics, extraction, orchestration, retry, pagination, cost, failure, provenance, or plumbing), then compare with ECDEV

coverage.read: src/server.ts (parts: tool list, crawl, scrape, usage and recovery payload sections, ~700 of 4,338 lines), src/monitor.ts (1-330 of 512), src/usage.ts (all)
coverage.not_read: rest of src/server.ts, src/tool-output.ts, src/session-credential.ts, src/introspection-cache.ts, src/research.ts, src/developer.ts, src/gov.ts, src/alexandria*.ts, plugins/*, docs, tests
coverage.statement: Bounded semantic review of the files named, not the whole source. No extinction is claimed.

rows.behaviour: Crawl scope is set by includePaths/excludePaths, maxDiscoveryDepth, sitemap (skip|include|only), limit, allowExternalLinks, allowSubdomains, crawlEntireDomain, delay, maxConcurrency, deduplicateSimilarURLs and ignoreQueryParameters. Semantics live in the hosted API, not in this repository; only the parameter contract is readable.
rows.failure_semantics: none visible: options are forwarded and the hosted service decides
rows.configuration: all optional; no defaults in this source
rows.ecdev_today: Frontier bounds depth, pages and URLs, is host-scoped, honours robots delay, leases one request per origin, and gives identical URLs one identity. No include/exclude path filter and no sitemap-only mode.
rows.knowledge: Path include/exclude and sitemap-only seeding are scope controls ECDEV lacks. Whether they would save requests is unmeasured: it needs a real catalogue crawl trace showing how many fetched pages fall outside product paths. The Scrapy study already measured that query-order and tracking-parameter merging join 0 of 2,586 live links, so ignoreQueryParameters/deduplicateSimilarURLs is not a gap on that evidence.
rows.evidence: parameter contract read; hosted semantics not readable
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: answerable with a live crawl trace; not run

rows.behaviour: Start returns a job id, the tool polls at a 2 s default interval to a terminal state or optional timeout, and firecrawl_check_crawl_status reads a job by id without starting or changing it.
rows.failure_semantics: a start with no id returns the response body as is; a poll timeout is left to the helper
rows.ecdev_today: ecdev.research.run persists a run with a deadline, ecdev.research.status reads run and frontier state by id without network, and an interrupted crawl reports CRAWL_RUNNING_OR_INTERRUPTED and resumes from the frontier.
rows.knowledge: ECDEV separates start from status the same way and additionally resumes an interrupted crawl from persisted frontier state with zero network calls; the donor polls inside one tool call.
rows.evidence: domain/commerce/src/service.rs research.status; resume covered by apps/server resume tests

rows.behaviour: A monitor compares each scheduled check with its retained predecessor. Page status is same, new, changed, removed or error; a check is queued, running, completed, failed, partial or skipped_overlap. Targets are scrape pages or search queries, with a plain-language goal, schedule text, timezone, email and webhook notification.
rows.failure_semantics: a check that would overlap its predecessor is skipped (skipped_overlap); partial is a status of its own
rows.configuration: schedule defaults to every 30 minutes, UTC
rows.ecdev_today: Watches are leased (a second claim cannot run while a lease is live), a failed fetch is UNKNOWN, a page is PAGE_DISAPPEARED only on HTTP 404/410 evidence, and a changed visible-text fingerprint is separate from changed bytes. Notifications are NONE by design.
rows.knowledge: The donor model is a subset of ECDEV monitoring on every axis read: overlap is prevented by a lease rather than recorded as skipped, and ECDEV will not call a page removed from an error, which the donor lets be one status among five. Not read: how the hosted service judges a change against the goal.

rows.behaviour: Every recoverable failure carries a stable code, request id, message, docs url, retry_after_seconds and, only where a retry can succeed, next_actions and available_tools. Quota and credential failures deliberately omit them so an agent is not sent into a retry loop. A failed credential check is a 503 with Retry-After and no WWW-Authenticate.
rows.failure_semantics: retry is advertised only when it can change the outcome
rows.configuration: retry-after 5 s for credential checks, 30 s for eligibility
rows.ecdev_today: Tool errors are code strings. Provider failures carry retry_after_header and retry_not_before_ms, and retryable_failure() decides which statuses may retry (checked against Scrapy this wave).
rows.knowledge: The principle (advertise a retry only when it can succeed) is already ECDEV behaviour at the provider layer, and it holds under the Scrapy retry oracle. ECDEV tool errors do not return next_actions; no consumer has asked for them.

rows.behaviour: Credits remain, plan credits and billing-period bounds can be read; each result reports creditsUsed; an agent run takes maxCredits (default 2500) and stops with stopReason credit_limit_reached.
rows.failure_semantics: the limit stops a run after the fact and reports why
rows.ecdev_today: Budgets are checked before a call in minor units; every provider call is recorded with cost, requests, bytes and latency; the default is zero paid.
rows.knowledge: ECDEV is stricter: it refuses a call that would exceed budget instead of stopping a run that already spent it. Credits are a vendor currency; nothing further to absorb.

rows.behaviour: firecrawl_scrape can return JSON matching a caller-supplied schema and prompt, produced by the hosted service from the page. firecrawl_map lists URLs without fetching content.
rows.ecdev_today: Extraction is deterministic (JSON-LD, microdata, OpenGraph, price parsing) with the literal source text kept; a main-content fingerprint separates page chrome from content.
rows.knowledge: Deliberate: a measurement path that asks a model to fill a schema cannot show where a value came from. ECDEV keeps the literal text and a hash. Whether model extraction recovers prices deterministic extraction misses is a benchmark question that would need paid calls and labelled pages.
rows.oracle_or_benchmark: answerable only with paid calls and labelled pages; not run

rows.behaviour: Anonymous use is rate limited per real client IP, converted to an account through a signup link; OAuth credentials are introspected with a short-lived cache and never fall back to a process-wide key.
rows.failure_semantics: failed introspection is a temporary 503, not a verdict on the credential
rows.ecdev_today: ECDEV holds provider keys only through its secret boundary and has no hosted multi-tenant service.
rows.knowledge: Plumbing for the vendor hosted service.
rows.evidence: files named; not read in depth

rows.behaviour: Hosted provider catalogue, paper-index, developer-index and government-index search tools with feedback that can refund a credit.
rows.ecdev_today: ECDEV discovery is zero-paid public research; none of these indexes is reachable without a vendor key.
rows.knowledge: Vendor-hosted indexes and a credit-refund feedback loop; no logic to learn beyond what a key unlocks.
